parsed_response.reasoning: The Salesforce diff calls parseRefreshTokenResponse(accessTokenJson, salesforceTokenSchema). When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is set, parseRefreshTokenResponse substitutes minimumTokenResponseSchema, which only validates access_token plus arbitrary number-valued keys — instance_url, signature, id, etc. are stripped from accessTokenParsed.data. The handler then persists { ...accessTokenParsed.data, refresh_token: credentialKey.refresh_token } to prisma.credential, so with sharing enabled the stored key loses instance_url (and other fields), which a jsforce.Connection initialized from the credential key would need — breaking the connection. This mechanism is directly verifiable from parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts and the Salesforce CalendarService.ts diff, so it is a real defect (the 'sync endpoint ignored in Salesforce' part is a design inconsistency, but the instance_url stripping alone grounds the bug).

judged_text: Salesforce: credential key gets safeParse wrapper issues; with credential sharing enabled instance_url is stripped, breaking jsforce connection; sync endpoint path ignores CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the refresh flow always calls Salesforce directly via `fetch("https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token", ...)` and never uses the new `refreshOAuthTokens` helper, so a configured `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` will be ignored for Salesforce. Also, it parses the token response through `parseRefreshTokenResponse(...)`, which switches to `minimumTokenResponseSchema` when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` is set; that schema does not include `instance_url` and (as a Zod object) will strip unknown fields, so `instance_url` can be dropped from the stored credential key, potentially breaking later jsforce usage that relies on it.
